duplicates.description: Both: more supply of a product (flour delivery / unsold tyres) does not end scarcity; same reasoning, different object. V:1.1-002-WHY and V:1.1-003-APP also cover 'not removed by plenty/income'.

duplicates.recommendation: Keep V:1.2-P04 (distinct: region, information problem) and J:1.2-P03; remove J:1.2-017-EVAL as flashcard (move to task bank or drop; its content is Case 1 of J:1.2-P03).

duplicates.description: Both classify/describe a mixed system via private operation + public finance.
duplicates.recommendation: Keep J:1.2-015 (4m, explains allocation mechanism); drop V:1.2-006 (2m, subset).

Four near-identical 'Define X system' cards; different terms, no duplicate. 1.2-016 (mixed) answer wording is thin compared with revised 014/015 (private ownership / state ownership clause).

duplicates.description: V P03(c) (fish-drying cluster, further concentration) = J 012 (regional food-processing, volatile demand). V P04 (export-crop concentration) = J 014 (national specialisation, overseas demand changes).

Level rises but share falls (agriculture 200->220 of 500->600; manufacturing 200->240 of 1,000->1,500).

duplicates.description: Match remedy to cause of unemployment (skills vs demand vs season).
duplicates.recommendation: Keep V:7.2-P04 or J:7.2-P03 (both assess same matching judgement); keep cards.

OC calc (12 mats/6 baskets) -> B can still gain -> comparative advantage misconception.
Goods balance: define -> compute deficit 20 -> deficit widens although exports rise -> not whole BoP.
Natural vs total population change: concept (V 008), numeric misconception (V 017), full calc (J 008).

duplicates.description: Per-head real income: total +5% and population +5% (unchanged) vs +10% and +20% (falls).
Private vs external benefit/cost (J revised to label profit and garden damage).
duplicates.recommendation: Keep V:9.1-004 (definition); drop J:9.1-001 or merge as example.

duplicates.description: Reed harvest larger vs managed (003) and ban vs monitored lower harvest (004): same managed-use judgement; V 003 resource project with lasting harm; J P03 Case 1 repeats.
Tariff with review date and tax-funded path: J EVAL cards are Cases 2/3 of J:9.1-P03; V P03/P04 cover tariff and public provision.

Five 'Define A versus B' compound cards (two definitions in one 2-mark card): each answer needs two separate definitions for 1 mark each.
duplicates.recommendation: Split or reword so each card has one concept (see contradictions/language).

sequence.rationale: Syllabus order is by theme, but several topics depend on later ones. Learner-facing sequence should follow prerequisites: opportunity cost/specialisation -> money -> demand/supply -> elasticity -> labour market -> firms and costs -> scale -> market structures (3.5) -> price level/employment/output/trade -> policy and control -> population/living standards -> conflicts.

prerequisite_violations.note: Elasticity named in a 3.2 card; V:3.2-P03(d) asks whether receipts must rise, which needs elasticity.
Price index and real income are used in 4.2 before 7.1 teaches them.
Average cost and scale savings are used in 3.5 before 5.3/5.4.
MC=MR is stated but no selected card defines marginal cost; marginal revenue appears only in J:5.3-017 and V:5.3-022.
Trade deficit/BoP stability used in 6.2 before 7.4.
Policy aims are defined before the measures they rely on.
Scarcity/demand for labour used in union topic before labour market taught.
Exchange-rate effects on exporters/importers precede trade and market-force topics.
Higher demand raises price/profit (1.2) before 3.2; acceptable as informal preview only.

within_topic_order_issues: 3.2 selection positions 9-16 (J:3.2-007 excess-supply, shifts, diagram, both-shift) come before V:3.2-016 definition of excess demand (pos 10) is fine, but V:3.2-018 (positions 16) and shift cards precede the non-price determinant block (positions 17-24): order should be determinants -> shifts -> combined shifts.
3.3: J:3.3-005/006 (total revenue effect, pos 18-19) after calculation but V:3.3-004 defines total revenue at pos 4; keep revenue cards after elasticity classification.
5.3: J:5.3-004/005/006 definitions are 1-mark cards sitting after V:5.3-012 (TC) - define FC/VC/AC before TC.
6.2: tax-type cards (pos 27-42) follow policy/instrument cards; budget (43-46) and interest rate (47-53) appear last: interest-rate cards need 2.3 repo/central bank but not tax; fine.
7.1: V:7.1-008 (real income) placed after cost-push; real income should follow index and price level.
9.1: V 'Define A versus B' compound cards at pos 1-5 before the social-cost calculation cards.
cross_topic_chains_ok: 3.2 -> 3.3 -> 6.3 (price controls need demand/supply; revenue effects need elasticity)

contradictions.detail: V cards and tasks treat 'the domestic currency' as market-determined and moving freely (N$14->N$17 per foreign unit; 'its currency is market-determined in this illustration'), while V notes 6.2 line 27 and notes 2.3/7.4 state the Namibia dollar is pegged one-to-one to the rand. Learner can leave thinking N$ floats against the rand.
contradictions.fix: State the quotation as a third-currency (e.g. US$) rate in every card and add 'N$ and rand stay one-to-one'; keep 'market-determined' only for generic foreign currencies.

contradictions.detail: J repeats 'rand peg maintained' / 'actual Namibia policy must support the peg' in prompts; selection revisions delete it from 6.2-032, 6.2-033, 6.2-P03 and keep it elsewhere. Peg is irrelevant to the reasoning in 6.2 interest-rate cards and creates unanswerable side-conditions for learners.
contradictions.fix: Mention the peg only where it changes the answer (exchange-rate cards, 2.3-016 central bank); remove from interest-rate cards consistently. Namibia-specific monetary facts (repo near SARB repo, CMA) are time-sensitive and were not independently verified.

contradictions.detail: V deflates: pay / index x 100 (N$10,500 / 105 x 100 = N$10,000; V notes 7.1 N$5,000/125x100 = N$4,000). J compares with the same bundle: 10% inflation on N$3,000 means N$3,300 needed. Both correct but a learner meets two methods and no card states they are equivalent. The N$4,825 vs N$4,831 discrepancy named in the brief was NOT found in the 743 selected items, the packets, or the notes (searched 4,825/4,831/4825/4831 in packets and notes); cannot confirm which bank produced it.
contradictions.fix: Add one bridging card: real income = money income / (index/100); same-bundle test is the check. If a worked N$4,8xx example exists elsewhere, recompute with the index unrounded and state rounding.

contradictions.detail: J:3.3-010 answer prints 'PED = -5/10 = -0.5, magnitude 0.5'; V cards give magnitude only; V:3.3-019 revision accepts 0.5 or -0.5. Notes of both banks use magnitude. Different base wording too: V 'initial values', J 'original bases'.
contradictions.fix: Adopt one rule: ignore the sign, quote magnitude; use 'original (starting) values' in all cards.

contradictions.detail: V:3.3-004 'money received from sales, price x quantity before costs are subtracted'; V:5.3-023 'amount received from sales; price x quantity'. Not contradictory but two cards define the same term differently.

contradictions.issue: public sector 'owned and controlled' vs 'owned or controlled'
contradictions.detail: J says 'owned and controlled by government' (2.1-001 revised, 2.1-002); V 6.1-001 and V 6.1 notes say 'owned or controlled'; V:2.1-017 public corporation 'owned or controlled by the state'.
contradictions.fix: Standardise on 'owned or controlled by government' (covers partial state ownership) or explain.

contradictions.detail: V:5.3-P04 treats falling average cost from 'fixed-cost spreading or productive improvement' as a possible sign of expansion benefit without separating short-run spreading from long-run economies of scale; J:5.3-012 and J:5.4-022 keep them separate (existing capacity vs long-run, all inputs adjustable). V:5.4-025 defines risk-bearing as 'potential cost advantages' while the other five types say 'reductions in long-run average cost'. J 3.5 uses 'scale savings' before 5.4.
contradictions.fix: Add a V card (or revise V:5.3-P04) separating short-run average cost fall from economies of scale; align 5.4-025 to the LRAC wording; teach 5.4 before 3.5.

contradictions.detail: Revised answer puts MC = MR, but no selected card defines MC or explains MC=MR; 5.3 teaches only TC, AC, FC, VC, TR, AR, MR (J:5.3-017). V:5.1-P02(b) 'State the profit-maximising rule' relies on it.
contradictions.fix: Either add MC/MR cards or restate as 'output where revenue minus cost is greatest'.

contradictions.detail: Revised V:7.1-010 teaches 'borrowers repay with money that buys less' as a straightforward benefit, while J:7.1-008 and V:7.1-P04 (and V 7.1 notes qualification) say it does not automatically help (income, interest terms). Learner gets opposite emphasis within one topic.
contradictions.fix: Use qualified statement: benefit only when unexpected and nominal income rises; drop V:7.1-010.

contradictions.detail: Market and planned definitions (revised) include ownership AND allocation; mixed definition (unrevised) mentions only 'ownership, provision or intervention'. Marks asymmetric.
contradictions.fix: Revise 016 to 'market allocation with government ownership/provision/regulation'.

contradictions.issue: Define = 1 mark in J, 2 marks in V
contradictions.detail: Same task type 'Define X' is 1 mark (J, 15+ cards) and 2 marks (V, ~100 cards); exam parts for 'Define' are 1-2 marks (framework: 2020 P1 Q10/Q12/Q15 1-2). Inconsistent mark expectation across the sequence.
contradictions.fix: Set Define = 2 marks with two marking points throughout (J 7.4-007/009 and 3.4-001 already revised to 2).

contradictions.detail: 'Define A versus B' needs two definitions in a 2-mark card; answer strings are sentences of two clauses, some with weak definitional wording ('Public expenditure is government spending...').

V NI = GNP at factor cost minus depreciation (V notes agree); J notes treat depreciation as capital consumption but no J card defines NI. Both fine but V 7.3-010 GDP definition omits 'market prices vs factor cost' while 7.3-012 uses factor cost - a learner cannot reconcile.
contradictions.fix: Add one sentence on market price vs factor cost.

contradictions.detail: 6.2 teaches growth = real output; 7.3 says total real output rising does not prove living standards; 8.2 says per-head average unchanged. All consistent but five cards, three topics, no single statement of 'per head' reasoning.
contradictions.fix: Fold into one anchor card in 7.3 with three variants.

contradictions.detail: 'Define HIV and AIDS, showing how they differ' answer is a two-line definition (virus vs advanced stage); other cards present HIV status vs illness. Consistent; only note that V:6.3-013 REV example 'HIV status' and V 6.3-015 repeat.
J 4.2-021 originally tagged 4.2 but concerns mobility of labour (4.1 content): objective tag mismatch in J.
contradictions.fix: Retag, then drop as duplicate of V:4.1-006.

evaluation_quality.detail: Stem states no data and the answer is 'cannot conclude; check ...'. Economic reasoning limited to naming omitted variables. E.g. V:3.2-P04 'higher price enough evidence demand increased' answer: both demand-up and supply-down raise price; this is real reasoning, rated acceptable once; the other nine repeat the shape.

Data in stem, opportunity cost or trade-off made explicit (mobile library 15 vs 35 users; partner equal influence; N$480 job vs training); judgement conditional on stated priority, which is genuine economic reasoning.

J 7m EVAL cards give quantitative or conditional stimulus (N$30,000 vs 120,000; profit 400 vs 500; social net -1,000 vs 2,000); J:5.1-001 and J:9.1-002 are really calculation + judgement and should be labelled calculation first.
Two-case structure forces comparison of conditions (genuine analysis), but cases are written favourable/unfavourable so judgement is read off adjectives.
V:3.2-P03(d) asks whether sales receipts must rise after supply fall; needs elasticity (3.3) to give a reasoned answer, so assessed before taught.
For/against lists are generic ('limited market may leave capacity idle'); little tie to figures; transfer to a different local economy would need no new reasoning.
Duplicate judgement already assessed elsewhere (see duplicates).
2.2-P04 and 2.1-P04 pose real trade-offs with costs (subscriptions; profit vs affordable route).

template_reuse.issue: V essay_plan template: 'Evaluate whether [an actor] should [infer/judge/conclude] ... solely from X when Y is not supplied (9)'
template_reuse.detail: 20 of 27 V essay plans contain 'solely/alone/single/sufficient/enough evidence'; the model answer is always for/against/judgement plus 'verify the unknown'. A learner can write 'evidence is insufficient, check Y' without topic knowledge.
template_reuse.fix: Provide data in the stem and ask for a decision; reserve 'insufficient evidence' for 1-2 items.

template_reuse.issue: J essay template: 'Evaluate ... in two seven-mark plans. Case 1 ... Case 2 ...' (14 marks)
template_reuse.detail: All 17 J essays use case 1 = favourable conditions, case 2 = unfavourable conditions; answer is 'works if conditions met, not otherwise'. Reasoning is conditional but pattern-predictable (answer sign can be inferred from stem adjectives such as 'funded', 'credible', 'trusted').
template_reuse.fix: Mix patterns; remove adjectives that give away the outcome; keep one two-case essay per theme.

template_reuse.transfer_assessment: Cards in both banks are heavily anchored in small-business, Namibian-flavoured micro contexts. Transfer to unfamiliar contexts is tested only when stems vary the structure, not just the label. Strong transfer: mirror pairs (V:2.1-018 / J:2.1-002; V:6.2-032 / J:6.2-036; J:9.1-003 vs managed harvest; V:7.4-007 plus J:7.4-005 different goods). Weak transfer: where only the scenario noun changes (V:3.2-006/010/017 grid; J 3.2 roll family; J 4.3 budgets; J 5.1 pottery) or where the card result is re-asked in the task. There is no cross-topic task (e.g. 3.2 + 3.3 + 6.3 price control with elasticity; 7.1 + 4.2 real wage) and no unseen-extract task like P2 Q1/Q2 (real extracts with 4 sub-parts).
recommended_transfer_tasks: 3.2/3.3: price ceiling on a good with inelastic demand (new context, learner chooses the diagram)
4.2/7.1: pay rise vs index for two workers (real wage)
2.3/7.4: depreciation effect on exporter and importer of the same product
5.3/5.4: average cost at two scales plus integration decision

coverage_notes: Counts in selection: 145 non-flashcard items (V 95: 27 case_analysis, 27 essay_plan, 22 data_response, 19 short_answer; J 50: 17 data_response, 17 essay_plan, 12 short_answer, 4 case_analysis). Flashcards with tariff >=4: 112, of which 22 are EVAL (V 5 x 8 marks, J 17 x 7 marks), 77 four-mark MECH/INTERP explanation cards (J 66, V 11), 12 V PROC drawing cards and 1 J diagram card.

AO balance: V short_answer 100% AO A (19 tasks); data_response AO B,C; case A,B,C; essay_plan AO C only. J case_analysis AO A,B only (4). Against the specification grid (P1 50% A/16% B/34% C; P2 28/35/37), the task bank over-weights C (44 essay plans + 39 data tasks end in judgement) and has no P1-Section-A-style mixed short items or cross-topic P1-Section-B tasks.

Topic balance does not follow examined mark share (framework section 3): 3.1 (0.2% of marks) and 3.5 (0.2%) have 4 and 7 tasks; 6.2 (7.9%), 8.1 (7.0%, 6 tasks fine), 9.1 (5.9%, 5), 2.1 (5.4%, 3 tasks), 7.2 (5.1%, 7) and 6.1 (3.3% with 20 marks in 2020 P1, only 2 tasks) are lightly covered; 1.1 (2.1%) has 3, 1.3 has 3, J has none for 1.1, 1.3, 2.1(except EVAL), 5.3 (JP02 only), 5.4, 6.1(P02 only).

Format fidelity: P2 Q1 compulsory is 20 marks with parts [4],[2],[1],[4],[9] on a real extract (2023 P2 Q1); P2 Section B parts are mostly 7 marks (44 parts) and 4, 6, 3, 2. V (6,7,7)/(2,4,7,7) and J (6,7,7) skeletons use plausible 6/7 parts but invent 7-mark diagram and analysis parts; 9-mark evaluate parts occur twice in ten papers; J 14-mark structures never occur.

Command words: V uses Describe, Explain, Examine, Suggest, Discuss, Evaluate in 20-mark tasks - mostly in the exam repertoire (Describe 4, Discuss 3, Explain 3 at 6 marks; Discuss 10, Explain 7, Evaluate 5, Analyse 4, Examine 3 at 7). J uses Describe three features (6), Explain, Discuss, Evaluate two plans. 'Suggest' and 'Examine' are examples where the syllabus definition is missing/different.

Stimulus sufficiency: V P01 data are sufficient; V P03/P04 omit data deliberately (14 tasks) so 'no cost figures' leads to non-numerical answers; J P02 tasks give full data but reuse card data. No task uses a real extract with line references as in P2 Q1/Q2.

Mark allocation checks: the sum of printed marks equals the tariff in every one of the 145 tasks (V P02 8x2=16; J P01 4x2=8; (6,7,7)=20; (2,4,7,7)=20; J 6/4/4=14); essay plans (V 9, J 14) print no sub-marks in the prompt but marking guidance gives 4/4/1 and 7+7. Not an error.

Verdict counts for tasks from stage-1: 76 KEEP_UNCHANGED, 69 KEEP_REVISE, none removed there - stage-1 auditors did not apply the 'bundle duplicates cards' test, hence the recommendation to remove P02 and J P01 reuse.

read.method: All 743 selected rows read in selection order (prompt up to 300 chars, answer 230 chars, revision up to 350 chars; full text for V:3.2-P01/P03/P04 and V:1.1-P04); mark sums for 145 tasks checked programmatically; 28 numeric/diagram answers recomputed (listed in notes). Prompts were truncated, so wording after 300 characters in long tasks was not read for every row; item-level defects belong to stage-1.
